Hepsiburada, 19 Kasım Dünya Girişimci Kadınlar Günü’nde, dokuz yıldır sürdürdüğü Girişimci Kadınlara Teknoloji Gücü programının sonuçlarını paylaştı. 2017 yılında başlayan programla bugüne kadar 75 binden fazla girişimci kadına ve 340’ı aşkın kadın kooperatifine ulaşan Hepsiburada, kadınların dijital ekonomiye katılımını ve işlerini büyütmelerini desteklemeye devam ediyor.
Hepsiburada’nın 2017 yılında hayata geçirdiği Girişimci Kadınlara Teknoloji Gücü programı, kadınların e-ticarette işlerini kurmalarına ve büyütmelerine destek olmayı sürdürüyor. Komisyon indirimleri, kadın kooperatiflerine süresiz kargo desteği, reklam avantajları, ürün fotoğrafçılığı, eğitim ve mentörlük gibi pek çok destek sunan program sayesinde bugüne kadar 8 binden fazla kadın kendi markasını kurdu. Bugün Hepsiburada’daki iş ortaklarının yüzde 25’ini girişimci kadınlar oluştururken, girişimci kadınların ve kadın kooperatiflerinin platformda satışa sunduğu ürün sayısı 134 milyonu aştı. Platformdaki girişimci kadınların cirosu yılın ilk dokuz ayında geçen yıla kıyasla yüzde 42, sipariş adedi ise yüzde 23 arttı.
Hepsiburada Kurumsal İletişim ve Sosyal Etki Grup Direktörü Canan Binal Yılmaz, programın dokuz yıllık yolculuğuna ilişkin şunları söyledi: “2017 yılında, bu topraklarda doğan kadın markalarını Türkiye’de ve dünyada büyütmek hedefiyle yola çıktık. Dokuz yıldır kadınların e-ticarete girişte karşılaştıkları engelleri kaldırmak için çalışıyoruz. Ancak bizim için asıl başarı, kadınların e-ticarete adım atmaları kadar bu alanda kalıcı olmaları, rekabet güçlerini artırmaları ve markalarını büyütmeleri. Bu nedenle programımızı yalnızca ticari avantajlar sunan bir destek modeli olarak değil, eğitimden mentorluğa, yeni pazarlara erişimden marka görünürlüğüne uzanan bütüncül bir yapı olarak geliştiriyoruz. Kurumlar arası iş birliklerimiz, kadınların başarılarını yurt dışına taşıyan çalışmalarımız, Anadolu’nun farklı illerindeki buluşmalarımızla girişimci kadınların dijital ekonominin güçlü ve sürdürülebilir aktörleri olmalarını hedefliyoruz.”
Hepsiburada, girişimci kadınların ve kadın kooperatiflerinin e-ticarette sürdürülebilir büyümesini desteklemek amacıyla ticari avantajlardan eğitim ve pazarlama çözümlerine uzanan kapsamlı destekler sunuyor. Girişimci kadınlara yüzde 50 komisyon indirimi, 200 ürüne kadar profesyonel fotoğraf çekimi ve sponsorlu ürün reklamlarında kullanılmak üzere 5.000 TL HepsiAd reklam bakiyesi sağlanıyor. Ayrıca ön muhasebe, e-fatura ve stok takibi gibi iş süreçlerinde indirimli çözümler sunuluyor.
Kadın kooperatifleri ise ilk altı ay sıfır komisyon, sonrasında süresiz yüzde 1 komisyon avantajından yararlanıyor. İadeler dahil kargo giderleri karşılanırken 500 ürüne kadar profesyonel stüdyo çekimi desteği veriliyor. Hepsiburada, ücretsiz eğitimler ve platform içi görünürlük imkânlarıyla da girişimci kadınların ve kadın kooperatiflerinin daha fazla müşteriye ulaşmalarını ve işlerini büyütmelerini desteklemeyi sürdürüyor.

The match between Spain and England took place at Atletico Madrid's Metropolitano stadium
England have been punished by Uefa following anti-Catholic chanting from the away fans during their Nations League victory in Spain.
European football's governing body have fined the Football Association £12,572 (15,000 euros) and imposed a suspended one-match ban for England away supporters.
BBC Sport understands the charge of 'racist and/or discriminatory behaviour' relates to chants that were deemed anti-Catholic and anti-Irish.
A further offence within the next two years would mean a ban on away fans is enforced.
There had been concerns of the prospect of racist chanting from Spain fans before the game in Madrid with England boss Thomas Tuchel stating he would remind his players of Uefa's anti-racism protocol before the fixture.
Tuchel stressed he didn't expect any incidents, but the visit was England's first to the Spanish capital since a notorious 2004 encounter at the Bernabeu was overshadowed by racist chanting directed at their players.
That led to a firm response from Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente, who said: "What I'd tell you, and you can tell Thomas, is that in Spain, there's no racism.
"Just like that, crystal clear. Just like in England, there's no racism in Spain. We aren't racist, any of us."
England won the match 3-2 to end Spain's 43-match unbeaten run and top League A Group 3.

Fenerbahçe 'nin yıldız oyuncusu Matteo Guendouzi, kulüp televizyonunda yayınlanan 'Günün Röportajı' programında açıklamalarda bulundu.
Bana göre oynadığımız bu iki maç gerçek anlamda kritik ve önemliydi. Çünkü taraftarlarımız aslında bizden bir reaksiyon görmeyi istedi. O reaksiyonu da taraftarlarımıza göstermek istiyorduk. Liverpool maçının zorlu olacağını biliyorduk. Ama kalbimizi, yüreğimizi ortaya koymamız, kolektif bir şekilde hareket etmemiz gerekiyordu. Bana göre de takım olarak iyi bir reaksiyon ortaya koyduğumuzu düşünüyorum. O maçtan sonra da Çorum ile bir maçımız oldu. O maçın da kolay bir maç olmayacağının farkındaydık. Zira kendi seviyemizi göstermek, sürdürmek niyetindeydik.
Millî ara öncesi iyi bir performans ortaya koyma niyetindeydik. Dolayısıyla bu iki maça bakacak olursak bana göre fazlasıyla pozitif noktalar ortaya koyduğumuzu, pozitif şeyler gösterebildiğimizi düşünüyorum. Elbette bu şekilde çalışmaya devam etmemiz gerekiyor. Çalışmalarımızı sürdürerek sezon sonuna kadar en iyi şekilde performans ortaya koymaya devam etmeliyiz.
Emre Belözoğlu'nu tanıyoruz ve pozitif noktaların ne kadar fazla olduğunu biliyoruz. Oyuncu olduğu dönemde de ne kadar büyük bir kariyere sahip olduğunun herkes farkında. Sizin de ifade ettiğiniz gibi oynamış olduğu pozisyondan ötürü bu konularda da bana göre çok faydalı oluyor. Antrenmanlarda bana sürekli olarak bu noktalarla ilgili olarak tavsiyeler veriyor. Kendimi geliştirebilmem için ne yapmam gerekiyorsa bunu benimle açık bir şekilde paylaşıyor. Bu tecrübesini de bizlere fazlasıyla aktarabildiğini düşünüyorum. Nitekim futbolculuk döneminde büyük bir oyuncuydu. Dolayısıyla bunların da etkisiyle ve sahip olduğu tecrübeyle beraber bizlere fazlasıyla yardımcı olabildiğini düşünüyorum. Az önce de ifade ettiğim gibi başarılı bir futbolculuk kariyeri vardı. Öyle umut ediyor ve öyle istiyorum ki teknik adam olarak da birlikte başarılar elde edebiliriz. Bana göre oyun felsefesi ve oyun planıyla alakalı olarak da önemli anekdotlara, önemli fikirlere sahip! Hem ofansif hem defansif hem de kolektif anlamda neler yapmamız gerektiği konusunda bana göre çok net, keskin planları var ve bize de bunları aktarıyor. Dolayısıyla hoca ile takım arasında iyi bir eşleşme, iyi bir uyum olduğunu düşünüyorum.
Tabii ki bizlerin onunla beraber hafta hafta, gün gün çok daha iyi bir noktaya erişebileceğimizi düşünüyorum. Performansımızı daha da yükseltebileceğimize inanıyorum. Onun felsefesi, oynatmak istediği oyun bana göre fazlasıyla takım ile uyuşuyor. Ben de bireysel anlamda çalışmaya devam edeceğim. Oyun felsefesini daha net anlama noktasında birazcık daha zaman gerekebilir ama bu konuda elimden gelenin en iyisini yapacağım.
Bizim açımızdan millî ara çok önemliydi. Çünkü hoca ile çalışma fırsatımız oldu. Zira yapmak istediğimiz şeyleri, onun bizden beklediği şeyleri otomatikleştirebilme noktasında, taktiksel anlayışını benimseyebilme ve bunu gösterip çalışabilme anlamında fazlasıyla verimli oldu. Kolektif anlamda bunu anlayabilme, çalışabilme anlamında bana göre çok önemliydi. Millî aranın bize iyi geldiğini düşünüyorum. Faydalı geçtiğini söyleyebilirim. Tabii ki hocamızla ile bu süre içerisinde zaman geçirerek onun taktiksel mantalitesini, taktiksel anlayışını da kavramış oluyoruz. Kocaelispor maçının zorlu olacağını düşünüyorum. Çünkü kaliteli bir takıma karşı oynayacağımız kanaatindeyim. Oynaması zorlu bir rakibe karşı oynayacağız. Ama bizler tabii ki hazırız. Oyunumuz belli, oyun stilimiz belli. Bunları da sahada yansıtmak istiyoruz. Oraya elbette ki 3 puanı ve galibiyeti almak için gideceğiz. Her hâlükârda elimizden gelenin en iyisini ortaya koyacağız. Her şeyimizi vereceğiz ve tabiri caize yüzde bin bunu hep beraber ortaya koyacağız.
Taraftarlarımıza söyleyebileceğim şey şu: Onlar gerçek anlamda sıra dışılar! Zira her zaman arkamızdalar ve desteklerini sürdürüyorlar; iyi bir maç oynadığımızda da, kötü bir maç oynadığımızda da, zor zamanlarda da… Elbette ki hayâl kırıklığı yaşıyorlar, sinirleniyorlar, kızıyorlar, üzülüyorlar ama neticede günün sonunda bizlere her zaman destek oluyorlar. Biz de onlardan aldığımız bu destek ve güçle beraber kafamızı kaldırıyoruz. Ki kafamızı kaldırmamız gerekiyor. Biz, kalpten, yürekten bir şekilde onları mutlu etmek ve keyiflendirmek istiyoruz. Tıpkı Liverpool maçında göstermiş olduğumuz performans gibi en iyisini ortaya koymaya çalışıyoruz. Çünkü onlara pozitif duygular yaşatmak istiyoruz. Dolayısıyla şunu söylemem gerekiyor; onlar gibi taraftara sahip olduğumuz için gerçekten şanslıyız ve mutluyuz. Hem içeride hem de dışarıda oynadığımız maçlarda bizlere büyük bir sevgi gösteriyorlar, bizleri destekliyorlar ve bizlere itici güç oluyorlar. Bunu kolektif anlamda da bireysel anlamda da söyleyebilirim; bizler de kaybedince üzülüyoruz. Kötü bir netice aldığımızda yaşattığımızdan sonuçtan ötürü bizler de mutsuz oluyoruz. Umuyorum ki yaşatabildiğimiz kadar fazla, maksimum galibiyetleri onlara hediye ederiz. Çünkü istediğimiz ve arzu ettiğimiz şey bu! Hem kulübümüz hem de taraftarlarımız bunu fazlasıyla hak ediyorlar. Son olarak şunu söyleyebilirim; onları mutlu edebilmek adına elimizden gelenin en iyisini yapmaya devam edeceğiz.

England have been handed a ­suspended ­one-match ban on away ticket sales by Uefa in relation to “­racist and/or ­discriminatory” behaviour by fans at Sunday’s 3-2 Nations League victory over Spain. The punishment is suspended for two years.
Uefa has also fined the Football Association €15,000 (£12,500), with the behaviour in question believed to be the chant of “Fuck the pope and the IRA” at the ­Metropolitano ­Stadium in Madrid. A further charge in the next two years could trigger a ban on away fans for a competitive game.
In a statement given to the Mail, the FA said: “We will not ­tolerate this unacceptable and deeply ­offensive chanting, and will work with the police who attend all ­England home and away matches to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action.”
Uefa’s control, ­ethics and ­disciplinary body announced that it had decided “to fine the English ­Football ­Association €15,000 and to order against the ­English Football Association a full ­restriction on selling tickets to its ­supporters for one representative team competition away match, for the ­racist and/or discriminatory ­behaviour of its supporters.
“Said full restriction on selling tickets to supporters for one away match is suspended for a ­probationary period of two years, starting from the date of the present decision.”
The relevant article of Uefa’s disciplinary regulations reads: “If one or more of a member association or club’s supporters engage in the behaviour described in paragraph 1 [insulting the human dignity of a person or group of persons on whatever grounds, including skin colour, race, religion, ethnic origin, gender or ­sexual orientation], the ­member association or club ­responsible incurs a minimum of a fine and either a ­partial stadium closure or a ­restriction on selling tickets to its supporters for away matches.”

The match had been preceded by Thomas Tuchel reminding his players of the anti-­racism protocols , given the last match between the sides in Madrid, in 2004, had notoriously been marred by abuse aimed at England’s black players.
Last month Spain were fined £15,000 and ordered to play their next friendly with a partial stadium closure after discriminatory chants about Muslims during March’s match against Egypt in Barcelona.
Sunday’s chant is a staple for some England fans but sung relatively rarely in stadiums. Several more frequently heard chants target only the IRA, including inserting “No surrender” into the national anthem.

Manchester City have won the Premier League on eight occasions
Premier League clubs have voted to cover legal expenses for the organisation's five board directors if any of Manchester City 's sponsors sue them.
The clubs met in London on Thursday for the first time since City were found guilty of a catalogue of charges relating to the breaching of the league's financial rules by an independent commission in September.
City have appealed and maintain their innocence, with a sanction yet to be decided.
The club's sponsors Etihad and Etisalat have both said they are considering legal action against the Premier League.
At present, under the league's articles of association, a director is financially covered if they win a legal case brought against them by a third party, but not if they lose. The league's rules will now be updated to extend legal indemnity for chief executive Richard Masters, chair Alison Brittan and three other non-executive directors .
City and Nottingham Forest were the only two clubs that voted against the proposal to provide extra legal protection, with the other 18 clubs voting in favour.
Due to collective responsibility, it means that all clubs are now liable to cover legal costs that could run into hundreds of millions of pounds, raising the intriguing possibility of City being financially impacted by the legal action of its own sponsors.
BBC Sport was told that City's CFO Ingo Bank asked Premier League chair Brittan during Thursday's meeting if the proposal was a direct result of threats of legal action from Etihad and Etisalat, but she said she could not comment.
While Forest have declined to comment, their objection to the proposal is said have to been on procedural grounds, rather than due to any support for City.
The club did not believe that sufficient information had been provided, or adequate time afforded, for clubs to properly consider the implications of the proposed amendment, particularly given the potentially significant financial responsibilities involved. It felt that such a decision warranted more scrutiny and informed consideration before clubs were asked to vote.
An independent commission appointed by the Premier League found City guilty of artificially inflating the club's revenues by over £830m over a nine-year period in September.
The commission determined that the club arranged "sham" contracts with sponsors, which disguised funding from club owners the Abu Dhabi United Group.
Premier League CEO Masters said City "systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade".
In October, City sponsor Etihad Airways said it was considering legal action against the Premier League .
In a statement, the United Arab Emirates-based airline said it "categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements".
Etisalat signalled its intention to follow suit earlier this month and described the Premier League's verdict as "entirely false and defamatory".

Batman Sinema Derneği tarafından düzenlenen 'Bir Ömre Bedel Ustalara Saygı' programı kapsamında kente gelen ünlü oyuncular Meral Çetinkaya ve Nihal Menzil için ödül töreni düzenlendi.
Ünlü oyuncular Çetinkaya ve Menzil, Batman'a geldi. Batman Sinema Derneği tarafından düzenlenen 'Bir Ömre Bedel Ustalara Saygı' törenine katılan oyunculara ödül verildi.
Törenin ardından basın mensupları ile otelde bir araya gelen Meral Çetinkaya, 47 yıl önce Batman'da çekilen Hazal filminin set anılarını paylaştı. Çetinkaya, duygularını şu sözlerle dile getirdi:
''Dün bana büyük bir sürpriz yapıldı. 1979 yılında Hazal filminin çekildiği, zamanında Türkan Şoray'ın da ziyaret ettiği köye götürüldüm.
Aradan 47 yıl geçmiş, Batman'ın Gönüllü köyü bayağı değişmiş ve gelişmiş. Benim zamanımda çektiğimiz Hazal filmi setinde köyde elektrik yoktu. Vagonlarla ve tırlarla oraya jeneratör getirip çekim sırasında kullandık. Geceleri oradaki insanlar, benim şu anki şaşkınlığıma benzer bir şaşkınlıkla gece ışığı gördüler ve ilk kez ışıkla tanıştılar.
Dün filmin çekildiği köye gittiğimde bu benim için müthiş sarsıcı bir şeydi, bir dünyadan diğerine açılma anı gibiydi. Oradaki insanlarla filmi konuştuk, hepsi çok iyi hatırlıyordu. Filmi hala üst üste izliyorlarmış. Tabii ben çok zaman olduğu için unutmuştum ama onlar içindeki bütün oyuncuların, arkadaşlarımın isimlerini tek tek biliyorlardı.
Türkan Şoray'ın duyarlılığını ve bugüne kadar 'Türkan Sultan' kalmasının nedenlerini bir kez daha anladım, zamanında bu köyü ziyaret etmiş.
O dönem Batman'ın içini açıkçası görmemiştim, transit geçmiştim. Otobüsle mi gittik hatırlamıyorum, o yıllarda köy yolları çok kötüydü ama şimdi Batman adeta bir mega kent olmuş.''

Ünlü oyuncu Ezgi Mola, özel hayatına ilişkin aşk iddialarıyla ilgili sorularla karşılaştı. Oğlunun yanında bulunan Mola, konuyla ilgili açıklama yapmamayı tercih etti.
Ezgi Mola, eski eşi Mustafa Aksakallı ve oğulları Can ile İstanbul'daki Bebek Parkı'nda görüntülendi. 2025 yılında evliliklerini sonlandıran Mola ve Aksakallı, çocuklarıyla birlikte parkta vakit geçirdi. Ünlü oyuncu, bu sırada gazetecilerin yeni ilişkisine ilişkin sorularıyla karşılaştı.

2023 yılında işletmeci Mustafa Aksakallı ile evlenen ve aynı yıl oğlu Can'ı dünyaya getiren oyuncu, 2025 yılında boşanmıştı. Eski eşler, ayrılıklarının ardından çocukları için bir araya gelmeye devam ediyor.

Fenerbahçe'nin Fransız yıldızı Matteo Guendouzi, liglere verilen milli arada kulüp televizyonuna açıklamalarda bulundu.
Lige verilen milli ara öncesinde alınan Liverpool ve Çorum FK galibiyetlerinin önemini vurgulayan Matteo Guendouzi, “Bana göre oynadığımız bu iki maç gerçek anlamda kritik ve önemliydi. Çünkü taraftarlarımız aslında bizden bir reaksiyon görmeyi istedi. O reaksiyonu da taraftarlarımıza göstermek istiyorduk. Liverpool maçının zorlu olacağını biliyorduk. Ama kalbimizi, yüreğimizi ortaya koymamız, kolektif bir şekilde hareket etmemiz gerekiyordu. Bana göre de takım olarak iyi bir reaksiyon ortaya koyduğumuzu düşünüyorum" dedi.
Fransız futbolcu, "O maçtan sonra da Çorum ile bir maçımız oldu. O maçın da kolay bir maç olmayacağının farkındaydık. Zira kendi seviyemizi göstermek, sürdürmek niyetindeydik. Millî ara öncesi iyi bir performans ortaya koyma niyetindeydik. Dolayısıyla bu iki maça bakacak olursak bana göre fazlasıyla pozitif noktalar ortaya koyduğumuzu, pozitif şeyler gösterebildiğimizi düşünüyorum. Elbette bu şekilde çalışmaya devam etmemiz gerekiyor. Çalışmalarımızı sürdürerek sezon sonuna kadar en iyi şekilde performans ortaya koymaya devam etmeliyiz” diye konuştu.
Takımın yeni teknik direktörü Emre Belözoğlu ve oyun felsefesi hakkında değerlendirmelerde bulunan Fransız futbolcu, “Aslında çok fazla şeyler konuştuk. Zira onu tanıyoruz ve pozitif noktaların ne kadar fazla olduğunu biliyoruz. Oyuncu olduğu dönemde de ne kadar büyük bir kariyere sahip olduğunun herkes farkında. Sizin de ifade ettiğiniz gibi oynamış olduğu pozisyondan ötürü bu konularda da bana göre çok faydalı oluyor. Antrenmanlarda bana sürekli olarak bu noktalarla ilgili olarak tavsiyeler veriyor. Kendimi geliştirebilmem için ne yapmam gerekiyorsa bunu benimle açık bir şekilde paylaşıyor. Bu tecrübesini de bizlere fazlasıyla aktarabildiğini düşünüyorum" dedi.
Fransız futbolcu sözlerine devam ederek, "Nitekim futbolculuk döneminde büyük bir oyuncuydu. Dolayısıyla bunların da etkisiyle ve sahip olduğu tecrübeyle beraber bizlere fazlasıyla yardımcı olabildiğini düşünüyorum. Az önce de ifade ettiğim gibi başarılı bir futbolculuk kariyeri vardı. Öyle umut ediyor ve öyle istiyorum ki teknik adam olarak da birlikte başarılar elde edebiliriz. Bana göre oyun felsefesi ve oyun planıyla alakalı olarak da önemli anekdotlara, önemli fikirlere sahip! Hem ofansif hem defansif hem de kolektif anlamda neler yapmamız gerektiği konusunda bana göre çok net, keskin planları var ve bize de bunları aktarıyor. Dolayısıyla hoca ile takım arasında iyi bir eşleşme, iyi bir uyum olduğunu düşünüyorum. Tabii ki bizlerin onunla beraber hafta hafta, gün gün çok daha iyi bir noktaya erişebileceğimizi düşünüyorum. Performansımızı daha da yükseltebileceğimize inanıyorum. Onun felsefesi, oynatmak istediği oyun bana göre fazlasıyla takım ile uyuşuyor. Ben de bireysel anlamda çalışmaya devam edeceğim. Oyun felsefesini daha net anlama noktasında birazcık daha zaman gerekebilir ama bu konuda elimden gelenin en iyisini yapacağım” diye konuştu.
Milli arayı en iyi şekilde değerlendirdiklerini altını çizen Guendouzi, “Bizim açımızdan millî ara çok önemliydi. Çünkü hoca ile çalışma fırsatımız oldu. Zira yapmak istediğimiz şeyleri, onun bizden beklediği şeyleri otomatikleştirebilme noktasında, taktiksel anlayışını benimseyebilme ve bunu gösterip çalışabilme anlamında fazlasıyla verimli oldu. Kolektif anlamda bunu anlayabilme, çalışabilme anlamında bana göre çok önemliydi. Millî aranın bize iyi geldiğini düşünüyorum. Faydalı geçtiğini söyleyebilirim. Tabii ki hocamızla ile bu süre içerisinde zaman geçirerek onun taktiksel mantalitesini, taktiksel anlayışını da kavramış oluyoruz” ifadelerini kullandı.
Ligin 12. haftasında deplasmanda oynayacakları Kocaelispor maçında galibiyet hedeflediklerini vurgulayan Guendouzi, “Kocaelispor maçının zorlu olacağını düşünüyorum. Çünkü kaliteli bir takıma karşı oynayacağımız kanaatindeyim. Oynaması zorlu bir rakibe karşı oynayacağız. Ama bizler tabii ki hazırız. Oyunumuz belli, oyun stilimiz belli. Bunları da sahada yansıtmak istiyoruz. Oraya elbette ki 3 puanı ve galibiyeti almak için gideceğiz. Her hâlükârda elimizden gelenin en iyisini ortaya koyacağız. Her şeyimizi vereceğiz ve tabiri caize yüzde bin bunu hep beraber ortaya koyacağız” dedi.
Devler Ligi’nde Shakhtar Donetsk ile oynanacak maçla ilgili de konuşan Matteo Guendouzi, “Şunu gayet iyi biliyoruz ki bu maçın özel bir tarafı var! Çünkü biz de aslında kendi evimizde bu maçı oynamayacağız ve onlar için de aynı durum söz konusu. Dolayısıyla bu maç için bir ev sahibi yok. Ama şunu belirtmem gerekiyor; iyi bir takıma karşı oynayacağız. Bireysel anlamda kaliteli oyunculara sahip olan bir takıma karşı oynayacağız. Zaten Shakhtar Donetsk’e baktığımız zaman onların her zaman için kaliteli oyuncuları mevcuttur. Kadrolarında her zaman iyi oyuncular vardır. Oradan Avrupa’ya transfer yapan, yapmış olan oyuncular olmuştur" diye konuştu.
Fransız futbolcu, "Bizler kendi adımıza iyi bir şekilde hazırlanacağız. Rakibimizi her zaman ki gibi ciddi şekilde analiz edeceğiz. Tabii ki zor bir maç olacağının farkındayız. Ama bizim amacımız ve istediğimiz kendi oyun formatımızı, kendi oyun stilimizi rakibimize dikte ettirebilmek, o dominasyonu sağlayabilmek. Arzu ettiğimiz şey elbette ki oradan 3 puanla İstanbul’a dönebilmek. Bunu yapmak ve başarmak istiyoruz. Şunu yinelemem gerekiyor; her halükarda bizler maksimumumuzu o maçta da ortaya koyacağız” diyerek sözlerini sürdürdü.

“Şunu net bir şekilde söylemem gerekiyor: Biz, oyuncular olarak kendi performansımızı analiz ediyoruz, kendimizi değerlendiriyoruz. Sezon başından bu yana bakacak olursak almış olduğumuz negatif sonuçlar vardı ve o sonuçlar daha farklı olabilirdi. Tabii ki o şekilde olmasını hiç kimse istemez. Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Manchester United head coach will be at Liverpool on 22 November
"We have to find a way to create the best habits and culture that makes us close to winning every single game."
Mauricio Pochettino has used his first interview as Manchester United head coach to outline his vision for the club.
The former Tottenham, Paris St-Germain and Chelsea boss wasted no time getting across the Atlantic Ocean after completing his stint in charge of the United States on Tuesday.
He met key staff on Wednesday, took training for the first time on Thursday and conducts his first wider media conference at United's Carrington training ground on Friday.
The 54-year-old is facing a packed schedule, starting with a trip to Anfield to face Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday.
Pochettino accepted a big challenge. United are 18th in the table. By 17:00 GMT on Saturday, they could be bottom.
So, what are the Argentine's priorities as he begins the task of trying to transform United's season?
"To create the culture is the most important [thing]," he told United's in-house media in a 15-minute introductory chat.
Pochettino's first Man Utd training session filmed by drone operator
Fitness obsessed & 'control freak' - what can Man Utd expect from Pochettino?
Matheus Cunha's injury-time goal against Roma on 3 November sealed one of only three Manchester United victories in 15 games this season
It would be easy to point to areas of the pitch where United have been deficient this season. However, it cannot be totally dismissed that virtually the same group of players were transformed over the second half of last season by the recently sacked Michael Carrick, who guided them to third in the Premier League and Champions League qualification.
Remarkably, Pochettino has won twice as many matches in charge of the USA this season than the three victories United have managed, with a 100% record from six games.
United, by contrast, have not won in the Premier League since August, while two of their three victories have required the Red Devils to come from behind. Their single clean sheet came against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah FK in the Champions League in September.
One of the most immediate tasks for Pochettino will be to alter the mindset of players who seem to have become restricted by the pressure they have found themselves subjected to.
"It is a mistake to see the situation," he said. "We need to see the potential of this club.
"We need to understand it is a game, and to connect with the game we need to feel free. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is our priority now; to work with them and take the pressure.
"Pressure needs to bring energy. Responsibility needs to bring energy because if not, it is too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back."
Diogo Dalot is consoled by Manchester United team-mate Joshua Zirkzee after being substituted during the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa
That said, there are some glaring issues that Carrick was unable to fix and Pochettino must find an answer to. The most obvious is defence.
The Carrick regime felt Leny Yoro was the player with the attributes - pace, strength and control - most suited to their needs. Yet, at 21, Yoro is prone to mistakes and he has also been needed at right-back because regular right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have, at times, been required on the left.
Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt have not been reliable fitness wise. Pochettino knows the baggage attached to Martinez, given his post-match criticisms of the club hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid, and the knowledge his fellow countryman's contract expires in the summer.
Harry Maguire has started all 10 league games this season but suffered a back spasm in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, immediately before the international break, and had to be replaced at half-time. Maguire has many attributes, but his presence does restrict the ability to press high up the field.
Ayden Heaven has made eight appearances in all competitions but has previously been regarded as being behind Yoro in terms of his overall development.
The 27-year-old was consoled by Joshua Zirkzee when he was replaced against Villa, such was the negative fan reaction to his performance, which included conceding a penalty at the start of the second-half.
It can justifiably be argued if Dalot has the talent to match the 260 club appearances he has now made.
Dalot has been described to BBC Sport as having one of the most committed and professional approaches to the game, that he is someone willing to take responsibility, happy to play in unfamiliar positions if it benefits the team, the first to offer support to team-mates, and a positive influence in the dressing room.
Liverpool and Man Utd fans give predictions ahead of Premier League match
Bruno Fernandes' alarming drop off in form has been one of the most noticeable features of the current campaign.
The Portugal playmaker has been a shadow of the star who scooped all the player of the year awards last season and broke the Premier League assist record.
He was axed for the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth after criticising Carrick's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League humiliation by Como and seems to be affected by concerns around his future - his contract also expires in the summer, although United are almost certain to trigger their one-year option on the 32-year-old - and the summer arrival of Youri Tielemans.
For the short term at least, Pochettino must decide whether to pick Fernandes in his favoured number 10 role and work around that, or drop him deeper, as Ruben Amorim did, or play him wide, which has not brought the best out of him.
Fernandes' status affects other areas. Carrick never seemed convinced by Andrey Santos, a £50m summer arrival from Chelsea. But with £70m Carlos Baleba out for an extended period, a partner needs to be found in midfield for Kobbie Mainoo.
Tielemans did not seem to have the running ability for the role, and Amorim wouldn't pick Mainoo with Fernandes.
Further forward, with Benjamin Sesko out, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo have tended to be used in the number nine role. But Cunha likes to drop deep, while, after a bright start to the season, Mbeumo has scored twice in his past 12 appearances.
Neither Shea Lacey nor Harry Amass have started a Premier League game this season. Both caught the eye on England Under-20 duty during the international break. Pochettino has history for giving young players a chance and the pair could benefit from that.
Manchester United co-chair Avram Glazer and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe have been the subject of numerous supporter protests and chants
There is one issue Pochettino mentioned in his interview he will soon discover requires delicate handling.
United's match-going fans have stood by every manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired. There is no reason to think that will change now.
However, their relationship with the club's ownership is fractured, possibly beyond repair. Fresh accounts to 30 September show the club's overall debt remains more than £1.1bn and a further £14.5m was spent on finance costs in the previous quarter.
This fuels discontent in the stands, already heightened because of various ticketing measures, none of which are viewed by most supporters as being positive.
"Chemistry is really important, chemistry between us and the staff and the fans and the players, the directors, the owners and everything."

New Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino (right) worked with his full squad for the first time on Thursday
Manchester United fans have been given a unique and unexpected insight into Mauricio Pochettino's first training session after footage was captured by a drone flown next to the club's Carrington training ground.
Twelve minutes of the session was filmed by a drone operator and uploaded onto YouTube.
Pochettino and his players, who were split into three groups, are clearly visible, with the session filmed from a variety of angles and distances.
"For the people asking about legality. It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it," said the drone operator.
"The drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn't fly over anyone or even near anyone so was a perfectly legal flight going by the CAA rules that regulates drone usage.
"The drone is correctly labelled, and I hold all the relevant licences, public liability and insurance required. As for leaking team news/tactics, it was half an hour into the managers first training session, there are many media there so certainly won't be the only footage of training released."
The session was also filmed by United's own media channel, who regularly film club training sessions.
Civil Aviation Authority guidelines include the following warning: "If you use these devices where people can expect privacy, such as inside their home or garden, you're likely to be breaking data protection laws."
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino (second right) hugs forward Bryan Mbeumo
There were 10 outfield players working with Pochettino, although it seems unlikely it will be the starting line-up for Sunday's trip to Liverpool.
While Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are regular starters, Ayden Heaven and Andrey Santos have had less involvement, and neither Joshua Zirkzee nor Harry Amass have started a Premier League game this season. Jaume Camacho 17, who is yet to feature at senior level, was also with the group.
On an adjoining pitch, skipper Bruno Fernandes is shown in one group playing the 'rondos' game, where two players are in the middle trying to intercept the passes of the five players in a circle on the outside. Youngster Shea Lacey and last season's FA Youth Cup-winning skipper Dan Armer are also involved, along with England youth international Bendito Mantato.
Next to that is another group which includes more experienced players in Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount, Leny Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.
The identical twins Jack and Tyler Fletcher are split between the two groups, with Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez across both.
Not all the players were identifiable and United confirmed defender Patrick Dorgu was involved.

Clubs rallied behind the Premier League’s leadership in a key vote on Thursday, overwhelmingly backing new rules that would protect the chief executive, Richard Masters, from potentially damaging lawsuits.
A vote to expand the legal indemnity afforded to Premier League directors was won 18-2 at a shareholders’ meeting in central London, granting Masters and other figures greater protection in the event they were subjected to legal action as a consequence of doing their job.
Manchester City are understood to be one of two clubs to vote against the extension of indemnity, and one unnamed side spoke out at length against the measures during the meeting. The other vote against was by Nottingham Forest, who felt insufficient time had been granted to consider the proposal.
The rule change follows reports that the organisation’s leadership may be named in possible legal action by City’s Abu Dhabi sponsors, who have claimed their reputations were damaged as a result of the excoriating verdict of an independent commission regarding City’s breaches of the league’s financial rules. City have appealed against the verdict.
This week the Abu Dhabi telecommunications giant and City sponsor Etisalat released a statement describing the contents of the verdict as “entirely false and defamatory”. Referring to the independent commission’s report as “the published findings of the English Premier League”, Etisalat said it was “actively considering all options relating to its rights and associated legal remedies in this matter”.
The details of any increase of indemnity, including who would cover any potential costs, were not discussed in the meeting.
The chief refereeing officer of Pro Ref, Howard Webb, attended and came under sustained questioning from club executives over recent referee and video assistant referee failures.
A report by the independent key match incidents panel this week found there had been two serious mistakes that were not corrected by the VAR during the most recent round of matches. Webb is understood to have acknowledged that performance in matchday 10 had been “poor” but argued that apart from that weekend, key metrics on decision-making had been trending in the right direction this season.
The Premier League has confirmed next season will begin on Friday 13 August and finish on 21 May. It said players would have 75 “clear days” of break at the end of the current season.

Thomas Frank replaces Frenchman Pierre Sage at Crystal Palace
Thomas Frank is happy to be "back in the circus" after speaking at his first news conference as Crystal Palace manager.
The 53-year-old, who was appointed on a two-and-a-half-year deal on Monday, has been out of worked since he was sacked by Tottenham in February, less than eight months after taking the job.
But, rather than dwell on that disappointment, Frank hopes to use it as a learning exeprience as he attempts to improve Palace's fortunes and lift them off the bottom of the Premier League table.
"If you don't learn from any of your jobs, I don't think you reflect, I don't think you improve, and I don't think you get better," said Frank.
"Of course there's a lot of things I have been reflecting over. The details, that will be for another time, but I can say I've learned, definitely."
The Dane said he could easily have extended his break from football, which he used to travel to Japan and Australia, as well as "visiting friends and family, eating too well [and] drinking too much wine" back in his homeland.
"I was very aware I didn't want to do anything in the summer. I put a statement out there, I needed more time," he added.
"I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it's good to be back in the circus, but it's also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.
"I was spending time with family and friends and doing all that, but I think the club, the way Palace is, how well Steve Parish especially spoke about the club and ideas, Matt Hobbs and Iain Moody and these guys, too, helped convince me it was a good idea.
"I'm a little bit surprised by this feeling I have in the body, how good it feels."
Frank's Palace reign begins with a trip to Coventry City on Saturday (15:00 GMT) and he says he returns to the dugout unbruised despite the way his stint at Spurs ended.
"I think we all have an ego," the former Brentford boss said. "Some are better at controlling it than others. For me, it's not the critics, it's more what I can learn, what I can prove, how I can get better.
"There's a lot of clever people out there, but the interesting thing is they only know 10 per cent of the truth. That's a tenth of the truth at Brentford , there's a tenth of the truth at Tottenham , and that's just the way it is.
"If you can't handle that as a coach or a player, then you shouldn't be in this business, and I'm very happy to be back in the game."
Why Frank at Tottenham was a gamble that ended in bitter failure

Thomas Frank has admitted he has a point to prove on his return to management as he aims to steer Crystal Palace away from relegation trouble after taking over as manager.
The Dane was confirmed as Pierre Sage’s successor on Monday with Palace at the bottom of the table after 10 matches having conceded 24 goals – the most in the Premier League. They face a crucial trip to Coventry on Saturday and Frank admitted he had been “surprised about how good it feels” after returning to work for the first time since being sacked by Tottenham in February .
The 53-year-old spent most of the intervening period travelling, working as a pundit at the World Cup and taking in trips to Japan, Australia and his native Denmark, where he was visiting friends and family when he received the SOS call from Palace last week. Frank previously spent seven years in charge of Brentford but left Spurs after just eight months with a win ratio of 34.2% – the worst of any permanent manager in the club’s history. He believes he has learned from that experience.
“I think you’ve all got an ego,” he said. “Some are better at controlling it than others. For me, it’s not the critics. It’s more what I can bring myself, what I can learn, what I can prove, how I can get better. I think that’s the big thing.
“In this world there’s a lot of clever people out there. But they only know a 10th of the truth. And that’s a 10th of the truth at Brentford and a 10th of the truth at Tottenham. That’s just the way it is – if you can’t handle that as a coach or a player or whatever, then you shouldn’t be in this business. I’m just very happy to be back in the game, very happy to be in a fantastic club, at Palace, where you walk in the door and you just feel the energy. You feel the people. It just feels good.”
Frank said he is planning to pick Roy Hodgson’s brains in the coming days after recalling a conversation they had when the former England and Palace manager was still at Selhurst Park.
“I was thinking, does it ever go away? The worry, do you get more relaxed about everything?” he asked Hodgson. “‘No chance, it’s impossible.’ I thought it would have been a little bit easier with age and experience. But in a way can’t help ourselves. I know what I want and the direction we should go in.”
Justin Cochrane – one of Thomas Tuchel’s assistants for England – has joined as first-team coach and took his first session with Palace on Monday less than 24 hours after the Nations League victory over Spain in Madrid. He is expected to be joined on Palace’s backroom staff by Bernardo Cueva, with Frank confirming that a deal with Chelsea is “very close” for the Mexican. Both worked with Frank at Brentford, where he spent almost nine years as an assistant and then manager. He is also hoping to add Andreas Georgson from Tottenham, who has been credited for his prowess on set-pieces: an area that Palace have struggled with for some time.

Frick has managed Vaduz and Luzern in the Swiss Super League
Aberdeen head coach Mario Frick says his track record proves he can produce exciting football - but for now a back-to-basics approach is required to save the Dons' season.
The 52-year-old arrived in the Granite City on a two-and-a-half year deal earlier this week to replace Stephen Robinson, who was sacked with the team second bottom of the Scottish Premiership.
Frick, who left Luzern in the summer after nearly five years in charge, has already identified a key problem he must solve quickly.
"I am known for high-scoring clubs. Twice with Vaduz we had the highest scoring record and last year with Lucerne, 76 goals," he said.
"I think Aberdeen is lacking goals [12 in 12 league games] so I am here to change that. On Thursday morning for the first time we did our attacking patterns and we have to improve now - we need time but we don't have it.
"More important now is to show the basics - body language, being willing to work, aggression, intensity - that is what I want to see on Saturday in Kilmarnock."
His first game in charge is a real baptism of fire for the Swiss-born former Liechtenstein player.
Defeat for the Dons would mean they replace their Ayrshire hosts at the bottom of the table.
The recent cycle of instability at Aberdeen is highlighted by the fact Frick - who was capped 125 times - has become their seventh permanent manager in six years.
But he is not daunted by recent history or by Aberdeen's situation - and sees similarities between the job he faces at Pittodrie and the one he inherited at Luzern in December 2021.
"I have had a very long career as a professional so I know the pressure. I am always an optimist and I know what I can do," he said.
"Luzern were at the bottom of the table with 18 matches and 11 points and the whole environment was sad and we saved them, so I am pretty sure we can do this also here.
"I am very ambitious. Now it is very important to get out of this situation but we want to go in the top six."
Across almost three decades of working in the north-east of Scotland, I have seen many Aberdeen managers come - and go. In fact, far too many to name check.
From this side of the microphone, first impressions are always intriguing - and not always an accurate barometer for how things will play out.
For example, I watched Neil Warnock cut an impressive figure at his unveiling in February 2024 and look how that worked out.
Well, having attended his maiden Pittodrie press conference, and observed him briefly at training this morning at Cormack Park - he exudes a calm authority.
He gives off the vibe of someone who knows where he wants to go, how he wants to get there and I suspect will probably not suffer fools gladly on his way to trying to achieving those ends.
Once both parties get to know each other a bit better, I also get the impression he will quickly command respect from the dressing room.
Frick appears to be a straight talker, and pretty clear in what he wants to get across.
While that obviously bodes well from a journalist's point of view, more importantly it could be crucial for the players as he looks to quickly deliver a winning formula that he, and the fans, hope can get the team moving back up the Premiership table over the coming months.
"With a manager change there is still a chance for every player to prove themselves, a new chance for everybody.
"To be honest I was really surprised with the first training session. It was brilliant and I saw a lot of quality.
"The facilities are paradise, it is incredible. It is better than in Switzerland so for me it is the next step. I am very happy to be here. I am very thankful to Adrian [Bevington, chief executive], Lutz [Pfannenstiel, sporting director], Mr Cormack [Dave, chairman], and the whole board."
"For eight years I have been a professional coach with only two clubs.
"Then I felt it is time for the next step. I waited for five months for this next step and when Lutz called me on Monday after the Hibs game I was excited from the first moment.
"I am really, really happy to be here because it is such a big club, such a famous club, a historic club, I am just proud to be here."
"Heavy metal, that is high-pressing, that is counter-pressing, vertical play, creating many goalscoring chances, that is heavy metal.
"In the next two weeks we have five games so I am just getting to know the new team and I have to make some very difficult decisions. But I am an optimist and I think we can do very well."

Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to "change things" at Manchester United; the Argentine insists his immediate priority is unlocking the potential of the existing squad and creating a culture capable of bringing success back to Old Trafford
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to "change things" at Old Trafford in a confident first interview as Manchester United boss.
In a sit-down with United's social channels, Pochettino revealed:
The Argentine arrived at Old Trafford following his departure from the United States national team, with the task of improving United's fortunes after their dismal start to the season. United sit 18th in the Premier League ahead of Pochettino's first game in charge, which will be Sunday's trip to Liverpool at Anfield, live on Sky Sports .
Pochettino believes it would be a mistake to focus solely on United's current predicament, insisting the club's potential, rather than its problems, must be the starting point for his tenure.
"It's a mistake to see the situation. We need to see the potential of this club," he said in his first interview as United head coach.
"It's about to start to act and to change things, and to try to affect in a good way all the areas, to try to really believe that we can recover that feeling about to win."
Pochettino has little time to settle in, but insists his priority is to create an environment in which United's players can express themselves and rediscover the feeling of winning.
"The most important thing is for us to start to work hard to recover that feeling. That feeling is about being winners, to win games, to perform. But that is not only to talk about winning."
Sky Sports News reported Pochettino is set to be backed in the January transfer window .
The club are targeting a left-back, centre-back and forward as areas to potentially strengthen. Pochettino is expected to have input on targets they will pursue.
However, with just over a month to go until the transfer window does open, Pochettino has emphasised how his main priority lies with getting the best out of the current squad at his disposal, as he looks to rectify the dismal start to the season.
United have 10 fixtures across all competitions before they will be able to add reinforcements in the New Year.
"The best request that we can have, the players that we have, and we need to love the players that we have," Pochettino added. "We need to support the players, we need to provide all the tools for their performance.
"It's only an act of responsibility now to start to work and provide them the possibility to translate all their talent on the field."
Pochettino also insisted he has the full support of United's hierarchy, despite growing tensions between the club's leadership, players and supporters.
The relationship between the board and sections of the fanbase has been strained by protests against the Glazer family and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, with supporters voicing their frustration over the club's direction, transfer strategy and investment.
There has also been public discontent from within the dressing room, with Lisandro Martinez directly criticising director of football Jason Wilcox following United's Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid in October.
The defender questioned the club's summer recruitment and said he expected more from "upstairs", specifically naming Wilcox before later apologising following talks with the club's leadership and Carrick.
Asked about the support he has received from senior figures since his arrival, Pochettino was unequivocal.
"I feel all the support. We feel all the support from the director and the owner," he said.
"And of course, now it's up to us to provide what they expect from us.
"We have a clear idea of what the club expects from us, and we want to be at the level of the demand of this football club."
Pochettino also stressed the importance of creating unity across all areas of the club, including the relationship between the hierarchy, players, coaching staff and supporters.
"We need to be united. Because in the end, we are Manchester United," he said.
Pochettino's first assignment will be a daunting one, with United travelling to face Liverpool on Sunday, but he insists his side will approach the game with ambition.
"We are going to go there, to Anfield, with the idea to win and be brave and to be Manchester United," he said.
"We need to make sure that we are brave and we are protagonists, and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool."
Pochettino also insisted it is the responsibility of his team to reconnect with supporters rather than place further demands on them.
"I'm not going to ask nothing because I think always we demand, demand, demand to the fans, but we need to provide to the fans before to the man," he said.
"The fans need to see that we are going to fight, you know, we are Manchester United and we respect our history and we are going to play for a win."
He added: "We are going to work so hard for you to feel proud about the team, the players and, of course, that is the most important, the club."

Blackpool have sacked head coach Ian Evatt on his 45th birthday after a year in charge following a run of one win and six defeats in their past 10 league games.
Evatt's final match was Saturday's 1-0 away defeat by fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon , leaving the Tangerines immediately above the League One relegation zone.
That defeat, however, came after the he said his squad had been decimated by a sickness bug during their trip to the capital.
Evatt departs the Seasiders with the announcement made a matter of hours after the club wished him a happy birthday , external on social media.
In a statement, the club thanked Evatt for his efforts and said Steve Thompson will take charge for Saturday's game against Wigan Athletic.
Blackpool announced Ian Evatt's dismissal less than seven hours after wishing him a happy birthday
Blackpool appointed Evatt, who won promotion from League One and the Championship during seven years as a centre-back for the club, as Steve Bruce's successor in October 2025.
During a six-year playing career at Bloomfield Road, Evatt made more than 250 appearances for the Seasiders.
On arrival as a manager, a tally of 13 points from a possible 15 in December 2025 lifted them out of the relegation zone, although they lost 10 and won two of their next 15 matches in all competitions.
They finished the campaign strongly, with six wins in seven games as part of a sequence of one defeat in 13 between mid-March and the end of August, only to struggle again as this season continued.
Speaking after their defeat by Mansfield in October, Evatt said he had "a huge amount of confidence" in his ability because of his record.
Evatt guided Barrow to the 2019-20 National League title in his first managerial role, then won promotion to League One with Bolton Wanderers the following season.
Wanderers went on to lift the 2022-23 EFL Trophy and reached the third-tier play-offs in consecutive seasons under Evatt, losing in the final in his final full campaign in 2023-24.
'It's been horrific' - Evatt says sickness bug decimated Blackpool
After an encouraging start to the season, Blackpool's form has been alarming since the beginning of September, and owner-chairman Simon Sadler has decided a change was needed with 33 league matches still to play.
There have been mitigating circumstances but everyone in the hot seat is judged on their points return.
His final game in charge will undoubtedly go down as one of those factors. Illness within the squad made the defeat at Wimbledon somewhat understandable, but the performance should have warranted more.
Throughout Evatt's tenure, he was forced to constantly juggle an injury list that never seemed to ease.
The centre-back position was a recurring problem and is unlikely to be solved overnight. Steve Bruce signings Fraser Horsfall and Michael Ihiekwe have yet to make a league appearance this season, despite being expected to play a significant role after injuries at the back end of the last campaign.
Supporters wanted greater tactical flexibility and a system that would allow mercurial talents such as Josh Bowler to have a greater impact.
However, Evatt largely stuck with a wing-back formation, believing he did not have the personnel to play effectively in other ways.
He made an immediate impact after taking charge, but that was followed by a significant downturn in form before a recovery that secured League One survival last season.
This term, there had been hope that those struggles were behind Blackpool.
Evatt will retain legendary status for his achievements as a player, having won two promotions and played in the Premier League.
However, Blackpool are now searching for their eighth permanent manager or head coach since Sadler took over the club in the summer of 2019.

The 52-year-old has replaced Stephen Robinson at Pittodrie; the Dons are 11th in the Scottish Premiership; his first game in charge is at Kilmarnock on Saturday; watch Rangers vs Aberdeen on November 24, live on Sky Sports
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Aberdeen's new head coach Mario Frick will not just be happy with Scottish Premiership survival this season, insisting he wants a top-six finish.
The 52-year-old takes over with the side sitting 11th in the table following Stephen Robinson's dismissal after their 4-0 defeat at Hibernian before the international break.
Frick, who played 125 times for Liechtenstein, previously took charge of the national youth teams in his homeland before spells with Vaduz and Luzern, helping the latter to avoid relegation.
"I had a very long career as a professional, so I know the pressure and I'm always optimist," he said.
Asked why he was confident of success, he added: "[Luzern] they were on the bottom of the table with 18 matches and 11 points and the whole environment was sad and we saved them.
"I'm pretty sure we can do this also in this place and I'm very ambitious.
"It's very important to get out of this situation but we want to go in the top six."
Frick will take charge for the first time on Saturday at bottom side Kilmarnock and he is determined to make an immediate impact with his style of football.
"Heavy metal," he said. "That's high pressing, that's counter-pressing vertical play creating many goalscoring chances."
Aberdeen have scored just 12 goals in the league this season while conceding 18 and Frick, who spent most of his playing career as a centre-forward, wants better.
"I'm known for high-scoring clubs. With Vaduz we had the goal record," the former St Gallen player said.
"Everything is lacking to score and so I'm here to change that.
"We have to improve now. We need time but we don't have, so it's more important to show the basics.
"Body language, willing to work, intensity. That's what I want to see."
The Aberdeen supporters booed Robinson off the pitch at the end of what was ultimately his final game at Pittodrie.
With just two home league wins this season, the morale of the Red Army is at a low.
Chief executive Adrian Bevington revealed Frick was the "unanimous decision," although his appointment took most by surprise.
"I'm not here to win with the fans, I'm here to win with my team.
"The supporters are amazing here I know that and but I'm not here to win them. The most important thing is the team and not me."
Frick faces an immediate relegation battle, starting with a run of five fixtures in just 15 days.
His first match is a trip to bottom of the table Kilmarnock. A win would move them five points clear, a defeat would see the Dons drop to 12th.
Next is a tough test against Rangers and former Aberdeen boss Derek McInnes at Ibrox, live on Sky Sports. The Dons have failed to win any of their last eight games against the Gers, losing to them in the Premiership and League Cup already this season.
There is no doubt Frick has taken charge of a team low on confidence, with four straight defeats ultimately leading to his predecessor's dismissal.
He has said he is "very hungry and ready to level up players" and, after playing most of his career as a centre-forward, he wants his team "playing forward and trying to score".
Time is not on the new manager's side. Robinson took four games before his first win, but with the prospect of ending the weekend bottom of the table, Frick will be aiming for a faster start to his Dons career.

Ukraine great Andriy Shevchenko has accused Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives of repeatedly asking for an employee of the country's football federation to "falsely" take the blame for the winger's positive drugs test.
Tottenham winger Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan from Chelsea , was suspended from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium.
The 25-year-old said he blames the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) for his failed drugs test and subsequent ban, believing it entered his system while on international duty.
In an interview on Wednesday, Mudryk firmly placed the blame for his 20-month absence from the sport on his national association, which has led to Shevchenko's response.
In a statement, former Chelsea and AC Milan striker Shevchenko, who is now president of the UAF, said Mudryk's comments amounted to a "baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally" and called on the player to retract his words.
He added: "His representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to find an employee who would falsely take responsibility for the meldonium found in his doping sample.
"The UAF refused, as such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work."
He added that "numerous investigations and audits" undertaken as part of the case were unable to shed light on when or where the substance entered Mudryk's system.
In his interview Mudryk also claimed Shevchenko had offered him little support, blamed the association for leaks that emerged during the case and said its handling of the matter delayed his return to football.
However, Shevchenko went on to say that national team staff had complied with a request from Chelsea not to provide Mudryk with any medication while on international duty.
And he also challenged the former Shakhtar Donetsk forward to provide evidence "to back up his words".
"Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps," Shevchenko added.
"These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine.
"The UAF completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk's representatives with the information they requested and remained in contact with those working on the case.
"I know the people who have worked with the national team for many years. I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism.
"If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question."
BBC Sport has contacted Mudryk's representatives for comment.

Premier League clubs met in central London this morning and voted by 18-2 to provide their board members with indemnity if they are sued individually in any potential defamation suits in light of the independent commission's finding the club entered into 'sham' contracts with sponsors
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Premier League clubs have voted to cover the legal costs of their five board members if they are sued individually by Manchester City's sponsors.
In September, an independent commission found City guilty of breaking more than one hundred of the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018.
City are appealing after the commission found they had entered into "sham" contracts with sponsors.
Two of City's sponsors, Etihad Airways and Etisalat, have threatened the Premier League with legal action.
Premier League clubs met in central London this morning and voted by 18-2 to provide their board members with indemnity if they are sued individually in any potential defamation suits.
City and Nottingham Forest are believed to have voted against. A two-thirds majority - 14 clubs - was required to make the change.
The board members are chair Alison Brittain, chief executive Richard Masters, and non-executive directors Mai Fyfield, Dharmash Mistry and Matthew Ryder.
Abu Dhabi airline Etihad Airways have sponsored City since 2009. In a statement dated 30 September they said the Premier League did not engage with them and they were not given the chance to provide relevant information.
Etihad said it was seeking legal advice to protect their interests. Etihad were not named in the 40-page published decision but they said it had "created damaging implications" for them.
Meanwhile, Abu Dhabi communications company Etisalat says it is are also considering taking legal action against the Premier League.
In a statement, the company said: "Emirates Telecommunications Group Company PJSC (Etisalat) views the published findings of the English Premier League, as they relate to Etisalat, as entirely false and defamatory. Etisalat is actively considering all options relating to its rights and associated legal remedies in this matter."
Sources close to Evangelos Marinakis and the Nottingham Forest board have said their decision to vote alongside Manchester City is in no way meant to show solidarity with a club that has been found guilty of serious financial breaches.
Forest and City were the only clubs who voted against the proposal to share any future legal costs which could be brought by some of City's sponsors who are threatening to sue the Premier League. The vote at the Premier League shareholders meeting was passed 18 votes to two.
Whilst Forest have declined to comment, sources have told Sky Sports News their objection to the proposal is procedural, rather than because of any support for City.
The East Midlands club felt that insufficient information had been provided, and that there wasn't enough time to consider the implications.
Forest felt that such a decision warranted more scrutiny and informed consideration before the matter was put to a vote.
The commission also said it was "regrettable" that a decision had taken so long to reach, with the hearing having taken place between September and December 2024.
A Manchester City statement read: "Manchester City is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League commission that has been published today.
"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.
"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.
"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.
"The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."
Manchester City's statement erroneously refers to a Premier League commission. It is an independent commission .

A 12-minute video of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session as Manchester United boss has been leaked online, showing the new head coach doing training drills ahead of Sunday's match against Liverpool at Anfield, which is live on Sky
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session today has been leaked online in a major security breach.
The 12-minute drone footage over their Carrington training ground was uploaded onto YouTube.
It shows Pochettino doing various tactical drills with his new team as they prepare for their clash with Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.
United have signs around the Carrington area warning that use of drones are "strictly prohibited" and anyone caught "will be reported for prosecution and subject to civil action".
The uploaders of the drone footage, CC Overview, claimed to have not breached any laws.
On the video they posted: "For the people asking about legality. It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it, the drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn't fly over anyone or even near anyone so was a perfectly legal flight going by the CAA rules that regulates drone usage.
"The drone is correctly labelled and I hold all the relevant licences, public liability and insurance required.
"As for leaking team news/ tactics, it was half an hour into the manager's first training session, there are many media there so certainly won't be the only footage of training released."
The training today was a closed session and not open to the media.
Manchester United declined to comment when contacted by Sky Sports News .
"This 12-minute video starts off innocuously. We see large numbers of Man Utd players on a separate pitch doing what is known as rondos, those small groups of six or seven players with one or two in the middle trying to intercept the ball. It's the classic pre-training warm-up. That's pretty innocuous. That won't give Liverpool or anyone else much of an insight into what Pochettino's tactical thinking might be for his first game in charge.
"But then on the next pitch, as the drone moves across, it zooms in, and the zoom is quite incredible. You can make out faces and we see Pochettino hands-on, walking them through certain match scenarios. At one stage Pochettino calls all those players in for a huddle and a briefing.
"I'm not going to give you any information about who those players are. But these 11 players Pochettino calls in - 10 outfield players and one goalkeeper. We shouldn't assume this is his starting XI, necessarily.
"Saturday would be the day we'd expect United to do their specific tactics and shape to prepare for the game at Anfield the next day. If this was drone footage of that session it would be even more damaging, even more explosive.
"But the fact it's 11 players separated from the group... it's a very difficult situation for Pochettino and Manchester United.
"I don't think [Pochettino and the players] were aware of it at the time.
"It's questionable whether the person handling the drone has done anything illegal. All around Carrington training ground, they have a large numbers of signs up saying drones are prohibited. But it's clear from these images the drone was not flying directly above United's property. It was to the side of United's property and zoomed in.
"There's absolutely no suggestion Liverpool are involved in this, they are clearly not. But you have to say, it could be advantageous to Liverpool and Andoni Iraola if he's planning his tactics for Sunday's game to look at this and get an idea of how Manchester United might be lining up and what Pochettino might be thinking.
"While it seems as though there are probably no laws that have been broken here, nevertheless it's an awful lot of very specific footage which Manchester United and Pochettino would not want out in the public.
"If you look at the impact of what we're talking about, Man Utd earlier today released some images of the training session and it showed Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu among the main training group. Both of those have had injury concerns of late. So those official images told me, Man Utd supporters and Liverpool's tactical preparation experts that Maguire and Dorgu may be in line for possible selection.
"It's gone a stage further now with this leaked drone footage because that has shed even more light on that. It gives a pretty clear picture of who's fit, who's out on the training field, who's involved and who isn't.
"That has to be a significant tactical advantage to Andoni Iraola and Liverpool as they go into this huge game on Sunday."

1970'lerde 15 kişiyle başlayan bir yolculuk, yarım asırda koca bir köyü başka bir ülkeye taşıdı.
Aksaray merkeze 22 kilometre uzaklıktaki Yuva köyünde yaşayanların anlattığına göre, gurbetçilerle birlikte yaklaşık 7 bin kişiyi bulan köylülerin 6 bin 500'ü bugün yurt dışında, büyük bölümü de İngiltere 'de yaşıyor. Köyde kalanların sayısı ise 500 civarında.
İHA'nın aktardığına göre Yuva köyünün İngiltere serüveni 1970'li yıllarda başladı. Geçim sıkıntısı yaşayan ve şehirde iş bulamayan yaklaşık 15 kişi, yurt dışında çalışma umuduyla kaçak yollarla İngiltere'ye gitti.
Orada iş bulan ve zamanla İngiltere vatandaşı olan köylüler, yakınlarını da yanlarına çağırmaya başladı. Kurulan düzen oturdukça yıllar içinde köyün büyük bölümü aynı yolu izledi.
Köyde yaşayan 24 yaşındaki Seher Sağlam'a göre gidenlerin çoğu göçmen olarak, bir kısmı da işçi olarak gitti ve ailelerini de yanlarına aldı. Ailesi orada olduğu için köyden gitmeye devam edenler de var.
61 yaşındaki Akif Çalak kendisi hiç gitmemiş ama üç çocuğunun üçü de İngiltere 'de. Ramazan Çalak ise köylülerin yalnızca İngiltere'de değil, Almanya ve Hollanda'da da yaşadığını söylüyor.
Köy Muhtarı Arif Çalak'ın verdiği bilgiye göre köyde toplam 800 hane bulunuyor, ancak bunların yalnızca 50-60'ında yaşam sürüyor. Köyde kalan yaşlı ve genç 500-600 kişi geçimini hayvancılık ve çiftçilikle sağlıyor.
Köyde bakkal işleten Ayşe Karapınar, kalanların bir kısmının da Aksaray merkeze taşındığını anlatıyor. Köyün en yaşlısı, 93 yaşındaki Cuma Okudan ise akrabalarının hepsinin yurt dışında olduğunu söylüyor.
Kışın sessizliğe gömülen köy, yazın bambaşka bir görüntüye bürünüyor. Muhtar Çalak'a göre temmuz ve ağustosta izne gelen gurbetçilerle köyün nüfusu 5-6 bine çıkıyor; gelenler bir iki ay kalıp İngiltere 'ye dönüyor.
Seher Sağlam da yazın köyde hep yabancı plakalı araçlar görüldüğünü ve köyün 'cıvıl cıvıl' olduğunu anlatıyor. Karapınar'a göre izne gelenlerin kimi köyde kalıyor, kimi tatile gidiyor.

NBA’de Houston Rockets forması giyen milli basketbolcu Alperen Şengün (24), Indiana Pacers deplasmanında ikinci çeyrekte iki gözüne darbe alarak maçı terk etti. Rockets, Şengün’ün sahadan ayrıldığı karşılaşmayı 119-104 kazandı; teknik direktör Ime Udoka sağ gözde şişlik, sol gözün korneasında ise çizik olduğunu açıkladı.
Indianapolis’te oynanan maçın ikinci çeyreğinde ribaund mücadelesi sırasında Pacers oyuncusu Aaron Nesmith’in kolu Şengün’ün yüzüne çarptı. Hakemler pozisyonu inceledi ve olayı normal faul olarak değerlendirdi. Milli basketbolcu kısa süre sonra sahadan ayrıldı ve takımının devre arasına 62-46 önde girdiği karşılaşmada bir daha forma giymedi.
Rockets, Şengün’ün gece boyunca oyuna dönmeyeceğini duyurdu. Maçın ardından konuşan Ime Udoka’ya göre sağ gözde şişlik, sol gözde ise kornea üzerinde çizik var. Udoka, bunun zaman açısından ne anlama geldiğinden emin olmadıklarını ifade etti.
Şengün sahada geçirdiği 14 dakika 10 saniyede 7 sayı, 7 ribaund ve 1 asist kaydetti. Houston’da Kevin Durant 21 sayı attı; Pacers cephesinde ise Pascal Siakam 24 sayıyla maçın en skorer ismi oldu.
Devre arasındaki 16 sayılık fark, yıldız oyuncusunu kaybeden Rockets’ın ikinci yarıdaki performansıyla final skorunda 15 sayıya indi, ancak galibiyet hiç tehlikeye girmedi.
Rockets’ın bir sonraki maçı Cuma günü (20 Kasım) Denver Nuggets’a karşı. Takım, Şengün’ün dönüşü için henüz bir tarih vermedi.
Yahoo Sports’ta yer alan değerlendirmede fizyoterapist Dr. Ribu Thomas, sol gözdeki sakatlığın küçük bir çizik ya da geçici tahriş olabileceğini, bu tür basit sıyrıkların genellikle 1-2 gün içinde iyileştiğini belirtti ve Şengün’ün Denver maçında oynayabileceğini tahmin etti. Daha büyük bir kornea sıyrığı çıkması halinde ise sürecin uzayabileceğini de kaydetti.
Milli basketbolcunun durumunun Cuma günü yayımlanacak sakatlık raporuyla netleşmesi bekleniyor.

Arsenal’s hopes of earning automatic progression to the Champions League quarter-finals were dashed by OL Lyonnes , as the French side continued their statement form in Europe.
Goals in either half from Jule Brand and Melchie Dumornay were the difference at Meadow Park and Lyonnes are top of the table and still yet to concede in the league phase with one game remaining.
It feels like Lyonnes are playing with a fire and intensity fueled by their loss to Barcelona in May’s Champions League final. They look a more formidable, coherent and hungry side, on a mission to end a four-year run without lifting the trophy they won eight times in a 12-year period between 2011 and 2022.
The visit of the eight-time European champions was always going to be challenging for the Gunners and based on current form getting a result would be even tougher. Last season’s runners-up had scored 20 goals without conceding in their first four Champions League matches prior to their trip to Borehamwood and they have scored 49 in their nine Première Ligue games.
The lack of competitiveness in the France top flight also means they were able to rotate heavily at the weekend between their two European games. Jonatan Giráldez made 11 changes for their 1-0 defeat of Saint-Malo on Saturday before returning to his first-choice lineup against the 2025 Champions League winners.
Clàudia Pina scored a hat-trick as Barcelona thrashed Servette 6-0 to go top of the Women’s Champions League standings. While Lyon were winning 2-0 at Arsenal , Barça edged clear at the top on goal difference as they dismantled their Swiss visitors.
Aitana Bonmatí fired in the opener in the 19th minute and then turned provider for Pina to drill home her first goal.
Esmee Brugts headed in a third in the 32nd minute, and Barça had their fourth just after the hour, with Caroline Graham Hansen hitting an emphatic penalty after Bénédicte Simon fouled Brugts.
Pina got her second in the 77th minute and tucked in from Brugts’s pull-back to complete her hat-trick late on.
Bayern Munich are two points behind after cruising to a 4-0 win over Austria Vienna . Klara Buhl headed the visitors in front after 27 minutes before Pernille Harder doubled the lead in first-half stoppage time.
Alara Sehitler’s stunning strike made it 3-0 with 15 minutes to go before Sophie Proost added a fourth in stoppage time.
Sofia Jahnukainen struck in stoppage time as Roma snatched a 3-2 win away to Benfica . Kayleigh van Dooren twice put the Italians in front, but her first goal was cancelled out by a thunderbolt from Caroline Møller, with Flourish Sabastine equalising after her second.
Paris FC got their first win of the competition, beating HB Køge 2-1 thanks to Célina Ould Hocine’s late penalty. Catherine Paulson fired the visitors in front 10 minutes in, but Sheika Scott bundled in a rebound to bring Paris level before the break. Press Association
Arsenal were not afforded the luxury of an easy league match after their battling 1-1 draw against Barcelona last week, playing a critical and tricky game with London City Lionesses , which also ended 1-1. Renée Slegers made two changes to the team that hosted ambitious London City, with Ona Batlle having picked up a knock Taylor Hinds played at left-back and Kyra Cooney-Cross started ahead of Kim Little.
They had their backs against the wall at a bitterly cold Meadow Park, as Giráldez’s Galacticos controlled the game. The away team had almost 69% possession in the first half and amassed 12 shots to Arsenal’s one.
The surprise was that Lyonnes weren’t further ahead at the break, with Brand’s 24th-minute goal the difference, the full-back sweeping in Vicki Bècho’s ball in from the right.
Brand was back to haunt the Gunners, having scored in both legs of last season’s semi-final between the two teams, with the French side progressing to face Barcelona in the final with a 4-3 aggregate win.
Arsenal were better after the break, but Lyonnes soaked up a brief spell of Arsenal pressure, Marie-Antoinette Katoto the only player left forward as they banked back and crowded the box to give the home players few options.
They increased their margin and dampened the mood soon after, Tabitha Chawinga’s cross from the left was collected by Katoto and the France forward laid it off for Dumornay who took a touch before powering the ball into the roof of the net.
It was an emphatic and unstoppable finish from one of the best players in the world as a mist lowered over Meadow Park.
It was a testament to the relationship between the club and the fans that the crowd remained in full voice, they urged the players in red and white forward, the North Bank doing all it could to lift the spirits of their struggling side.
There were no more goals and Arsenal’s single shot on target was almost the last kick of the game as a controlled Lyonnes performance demonstrated the gulf in quality between the sides.
Arsenal need to quickly move on, with West Ham their last game before the international break. They had needed a win to have any serious chance of earning a place in top four, avoiding a quarter-final playoff place.
They now sit eighth and will face Inter in their final league phase match in December, with the Italian side needing a win against the north London team to keep any hopes of a playoff place alive. That will not be easy, but a seeded playoff place is in their hands, if they want it.
